acceptance_criteria: A disconnect shorter than every fallback polling interval still reconciles logs, chats, messages, feed, and access after reconnect.
A reconnect that occurs while a catch-up request is pending cannot cancel or supersede the proof of current data.
A failed catch-up remains visibly stale and retries with bounded backoff.
Server restart or stream-generation change forces reconciliation.
A sequence gap forces reconciliation, and duplicate or reordered events cannot mark data current.
Cursor-too-old and replay-unavailable cases fall back to a complete current-state observation.
Reconnect flapping is concurrency-bounded and does not create a query storm.
Every realtime-owned hook exposes observation age and stale or unavailable state appropriate to its semantics.
The connection banner and recovery toast cannot report full recovery before reconciliation completes.
The freshness guard contains no dead or already-compliant exemptions, and every remaining waiver has an owner and expiry.
README, public-surface, and realtime architecture documentation match the implemented sequence, reconciliation, freshness, and polling behavior.

falsifier_or_remaining_gap: An existing continuity contract would falsify the issue only if reconnect or a versioned hello detected missed generations or sequence gaps, retained or rebuilt a bounded cursor, reconciled every active realtime-owned query before declaring data current, preserved failed catch-up as visible stale state, and kept polling or another complete observation active until that proof landed. Exact pinned-source assertions disproved all of those conditions. The prior issue author reported a failing audit-only jsdom reconnect test, but this review did not recreate that temporary test because the assigned lane permitted mutation only of this review record; no new failing test file or temporary artifact was created. The current 162 passing focused tests prove stable current behavior, not absence of loss. End-to-end server restart, dropped-frame, cursor-too-old, replay-unavailable, reordered-event, failed-refetch, and reconnect-flap cases therefore remain implementation verification obligations. #2520 producer truth, #2521 bounded broadcaster lifecycle and write outcomes, and #2522 producer-cycle coverage must land or expose stable contracts before #2519 treats sequenced delivery as authoritative; #2518 may proceed in parallel but its logs/feed completeness envelope is required before those caches can be called current.
impact: The UI can remove its reconnect warning and emit a connection-restored success signal while logs, chats, messages, feed, access, or other event-owned caches still omit changes made during the disconnect. A short gap can reopen the socket before fallback polling fires, immediately disabling the backstop without a catch-up receipt. Operators then cannot distinguish no intervening changes from missed invalidations, failed reconciliation, or an unavailable producer, and stale access or incident evidence can persist until an unrelated later event, focus/remount behavior, or manual refresh happens to invalidate it.
lead_verification_obligations: Re-read the live issue identity, title, body hash, labels, timestamp, exact SSH remote main, and every open pull-request body, head, reference page, and changed-file page immediately before registry integration or metadata mutation.

Sequence the protocol work after #2520 producer truth, #2521 bounded WebSocket client delivery outcomes, and #2522 producer-cycle freshness expose stable contracts; coordinate the logs/feed projection with #2518 without combining their implementation reviews.

Approve one versioned envelope and reconciliation vocabulary covering schema version, stream generation, sequence, emitted time, event type, scope, gap reason, replay outcome, producer coverage, delivery outcome, and active-query reconciliation state.

Require RED and GREEN tests on the real RealtimeProvider for a sub-poll-interval disconnect, reconnect before fallback polling, pending catch-up during reconnect, failed catch-up, server generation change, sequence gap, duplicate and reordered events, cursor-too-old, replay unavailable, and reconnect flapping.

Verify that reconnect cannot disable fallback observation or emit a success toast until every active realtime-owned query has either a successful current observation or an explicit visible stale or unavailable outcome.

Require logs and feed to consume #2518's availability and completeness envelope, and require chats, messages, access, lines, typing, and search to declare their own complete observation or bounded recovery contract.
Verify retry, replay, invalidation, and reconciliation work is coalesced, concurrency-bounded, abort-safe, and unable to create request storms or let an older request mark a newer generation current.

Retire dead and already-compliant freshness exemptions, give every remaining waiver an owner, reason, and expiry, and add a fail-closed mapping from every realtime-owned query family to its backstop and reconciliation projection.

Update README, public-surface, performance, and architecture documentation only after the implemented event union, producer coverage, delivery outcomes, polling behavior, and UI recovery states are proven at the exact candidate revision.

Use reserved synthetic values in all protocol, event, cache, log, and UI fixtures; publish no live identity, message, cache content, connection detail, location, credential, raw error, or topology value.

suggested_remediation: Introduce a versioned realtime envelope and hello receipt bound to stream generation, monotonic sequence, producer coverage, and bounded delivery outcomes. Keep transport state separate from data-reconciliation state. On every generation change, detected gap, delivery loss, or reconnect, preserve polling or another complete observation until a concurrency-bounded active-query registry has successfully reconciled each realtime-owned family or retained an explicit visible stale or unavailable result. Make replay an optimization with a complete-state fallback, consume #2518 for qualified logs/feed observations, and retire stale freshness exemptions and inaccurate documentation only after exact RED/GREEN gap tests prove the full contract.
